title: Orgwide ops sprint retrospective - October 03 2027
content:
Context:
This was an orgwide ops-focused all-hands held Oct 3, 2027 (09:30-10:45 PT). Goal: surface operational pain points from the last sprint, align on mitigations for recurring latency regressions, and decide runway for the Dedicated burst-capacity pilot. Notes below capture the highlights, debates, and a prioritized action list.

Attendees (primary):
- Sofia Martinez (host) — Eng, Serving Runtime
- Ethan Park — SRE
- Priya Shah — Platform Eng (autoscaling)
- Marco Liu — Observability
- Dana Roberts — Product (Dedicated)
- Ava Chen — Solutions Eng
- ~40 engineers across serving-runtime, platform-engineering, observability (roster in Confluence)

Agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot (5m)
2) Incident and latency regression review (20m)
3) Dedicated pilot readiness + capacity policy (20m)
4) Observability & rollout improvements (15m)
5) Action items, owners, and deadlines (10m)

Metrics snapshot (reported by Marco Liu):
- Cluster p99 latency (tokenized generation queries) — 310ms (target 250ms)
- Median latency — 78ms (target 75ms)
- Request error rate (5xx) — 0.55% (up from 0.22% two sprints ago)
- Avg cost per 1k tokens served — $0.68 (in-scope for Optimize suggestions)
- KV cache hit rate across high-volume routes — 62% (opportunity: improve for short-context workloads)

Observations: the p99 shift correlates with two changes deployed during sprint N: (a) a kernel update for fused attention in the 13B family, (b) a default autoscaling cooldown parameter change to be more conservative.

Incident & regression review (Ethan + Sofia):
- Incident INF-3321: transient OOMs on n1-highmem pool (2027-09-26). Cause: a combination of slightly increased request batch sizes from the new batching heuristic and a lower-than-anticipated GPU memory buffer during rollout. Remediated by hotfix 2027-09-27 (throttle + temporary config rollback).
- Latency spike pattern: long tails occurred primarily on longer-context (>2048 tokens) chat workloads; these interact poorly with dynamic KV-cache eviction under memory pressure.
- Near-miss: an autoscaler oscillation on 2027-09-29 that created short capacity gaps for Dedicated customers in eu-west; auto-failover engaged but added ~300ms tail latency.

Key takeaways from root-cause discussion:
- Batching heuristic is optimizing for throughput without sufficient memory-safety bounds for some model variants; we need explicit batch caps per model-family and dynamic detection of memory pressure.
- The fused-attention kernel change improves median throughput on happy paths but exacerbates worst-case memory usage for long contexts; revert or add guard is required.
- Observability gaps: while traces capture token-level timing, we lack a clear composite signal that ties KV-cache evictions, batch size, and GPU memory pressure into a single alert surface.

Dedicated pilot readiness (Dana):
- Pilot target: 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated reserved pools by EOY. Requirements reviewed: SLA 99.9% weekly, private network peering, and dedicated autoscaling rules.
- Risk: current autoscaler cooldown/weighting described above creates oscillation risk with Dedicated pools if the shared routing suddenly directs burst traffic.
- Decision: proceed with pilot, but gating conditions must be met: (1) per-pool explicit throttle policies; (2) two-week soak test with synthetic workloads; (3) on-call runbook updated and runbook drills scheduled.

Observability & rollout improvements (Priya + Marco):
- Proposed short term (next sprint): introduce composite alert metric "serving_runtime_memory_pressure_v1". This will be a synthesized signal (queue latency > X AND gpu_free_mem < Y AND kv_evictions_rate > Z) to catch the pathological cases faster.
- Instrumentation: add a dimension to traces to surface batch size and estimated KV cache footprint per request. Marco will draft trace schema change PR.
- Rollouts: change default rollout strategy for fused kernels to "canary with memory-guard": 5% traffic for 48h with live memory and tail-latency checks before increasing.

Operational proposals debated and decisions made:
1) Batching: introduce model-family safe caps + heuristic change. Decided: implement caps and a transparent telemetry export by Oct 17. Owner: Priya Shah.
2) Kernel fused-attention: immediate action: revert global rollout, opt-in canary with memory guard. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Deadline: revert initiated within 24h (INF-hotfix ticket).
3) Dedicated autoscaling policy: per-pool minimum floor + slower scale-down (cooldown increased to 5m from 90s). Owner: Dana Roberts + Priya. Deadline: Oct 10.
4) Composite memory alert: implement and tune in staging, then promote to production. Owner: Marco Liu. Deadline: Oct 14.

Action items (prioritized):
- [A1] Revert fused-attention global rollout and open canary playbook; create follow-up PR to add memory guard. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Due: 2027-10-04. Linked: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/498
- [A2] Implement model-family batch caps and telemetry for observed batch sizes. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2027-10-17. Linked: JIRA-INF-3387
- [A3] Autoscaler policy change for Dedicated pools (min-floor + slower scale-down). Owner: Dana Roberts + Priya Shah. Due: 2027-10-10. Linked: CONFLUENCE-8572 (design doc)
- [A4] Composite alert prototype in staging + alerting playbook. Owner: Marco Liu. Due: 2027-10-14.
- [A5] Soak-test plan for Dedicated pilot (synthetic workloads + chaos injection). Owner: Ava Chen. Due: 2027-10-21.
- [A6] Update on-call runbook with specific failure modes (OOM, autoscaler oscillation, cache-thrash). Owner: Ethan Park. Due: 2027-10-07.

Parking lot / lower-priority items:
- Revisit kernel memory estimator model (research task) — assigned to research/ML-infra but deprioritized until pilot stabilizes.
- Consider token-level compression for very long contexts (exploratory).

Risks called out by the room:
- If p99 remains >300ms through Oct, product will consider rate limits on free-tier hosted routes to protect Dedicated SLAs.
- The Dedicated pilot timeline is tight; failure in soak test will shift ramp to Q1 2028.

Notes & follow-up coordination:
- Slack channel: #org-serving-allhands (thread pinned with recording + slides).
- Full meeting recording and slide deck uploaded to Confluence: CONFLUENCE-8572
- Jira ticket for the primary incident: JIRA-INF-3321

Next steps / next sync:
- Weekly follow-up: Monday 09:30 PT all-hands focused on action status until the critical items (A1-A4) are closed. Meeting owner: Sofia Martinez.
- Next full org all-hands (broad updates): Oct 24, 2027 (tentative).

Appendix (raw quick notes captured live):
- Marco: "we're getting good medians but the tails are creeping — KV eviction patterns align to certain customer jobs every night"
- Ethan: "autoscaler change was well-intentioned to reduce flapping but we overshot the cooldown"
- Dana: "we can gate Dedicated traffic routing on a simple capacity-credits scheme if needed"
- Priya: "batch caps will be conservative at first; we can loosen after we get telemetry"

End of notes. Please add review comments inline in this doc and tag owners in the relevant action items.
